Series::clear¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

void Series::clear() const

What It Does¶

clear() removes the currently stored reverse-mode sensitivity from this Series.

That is a narrower operation than many readers first assume.

It does:

  • forget the stored sensitivity value, if one exists

It does not:

  • disable tracks_slope()

  • alter the actual numeric data in the Series

  • remove the ability to build future reverse-mode graphs from this value

So the right mental model is “clear the stored sensitivity state,” not “detach this series from reverse-mode entirely.”

Parameters¶

None.

This is a state-reset operation on self.

Returns¶

void The method mutates stored autodiff state and does not return a value.

Mathematical Meaning¶

If a reverse pass stored dL/dx on a tracked leaf x, then clear() deletes that stored public result.

It does not change what dL/dx was for the already-run computation. It only changes what is still stored on the object afterward.

That is why this method is about bookkeeping, not differentiation. It does not recompute anything and does not change the forward function.

When To Use It¶

clear() is most useful in three situations:

  • you want to inspect one reverse pass, then discard it before the next one

  • you are reusing a tracked leaf across separate computations and want a clean stored sensitivity buffer

  • you want has_sensitivity() to become false again without disabling tracking

That last point is important. Clearing stored sensitivity and turning tracking off are separate controls.

Examples¶

Example 1. After a reverse pass, clear() removes the stored sensitivity and has_sensitivity() becomes false again.

auto life = pluss::make_series({2.0, 4.0, 8.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());

std::cout << "before=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
life.log().sum().reverse();
std::cout << "after_reverse=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
life.clear();
std::cout << "after_clear=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

The reverse pass computes a real stored sensitivity for the scalar objective

L = log(2) + log(4) + log(8)

and clear() then removes that stored result.

Output¶

before=false
after_reverse=true
after_clear=false

Example 2. Clearing between passes lets the next reverse pass start from an empty stored sensitivity buffer.

auto reuse = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
reuse.tracks_slope_(true);

reuse.mul(2.0).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "first_dL_dx=" << reuse.sensitivity() << "\n";

reuse.clear();
reuse.mul(5.0).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "second_dL_dx=" << reuse.sensitivity() << "\n";

The first scalar objective is

L1 = 2x1 + 2x2 + 2x3

so the stored sensitivity is [2, 2, 2].

After clearing, the second scalar objective is

L2 = 5x1 + 5x2 + 5x3

so the new stored sensitivity is [5, 5, 5].

Output¶

first_dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2]
second_dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[5, 5, 5]

The second pass is not added on top of the first one because the stored sensitivity was cleared before it ran.

Example 3. Clearing stored sensitivity does not disable tracking.

auto keep_track = pluss::make_series({9.0, 10.0});
keep_track.tracks_slope_(true);
keep_track.mul(4.0).sum().reverse();
keep_track.clear();

std::cout << "tracks=" << (keep_track.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "has_dL_dx=" << (keep_track.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

The leaf is still configured to participate in future reverse passes even though its current stored sensitivity was discarded.

Output¶

tracks=true
has_dL_dx=false

Example 4. Calling clear() on a series that does not currently store sensitivity is a harmless no-op.

auto noop = pluss::make_series({7.0, 8.0});
noop.clear();
std::cout << "has_dL_dx=" << (noop.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

has_dL_dx=false

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • clear() does not turn tracking off. Use tracks_slope_ for that.

  • Clearing stored sensitivity does not change the forward values.

  • This method does not recompute derivatives. It only removes the stored public result of an earlier reverse pass.

Summary¶

Use clear() when you want to forget the current stored sensitivity while keeping the Series itself and its tracking configuration intact.

See Also¶

  • Series::has_sensitivity: test whether a stored sensitivity currently exists.

  • Series::sensitivity: read the stored value itself.

  • Series::tracks_slope_: enable or disable tracking.
